what: Exercise 2: Naive vs. Classical Model Fitting
title: Unit 00: Getting Started
text: Using labeled unlabeled sets, fit two models: Naive OLS unlabeled set using lm() f ~ X1. Classical OLS labeled set using lm() Y ~ X1. what: Exercise 3: IPD Model Fitting via the PSPA Estimator
title: Unit 00: Getting Started
text: Let’s run one method, pspa, proposed Miao et al., 2024. PSPA estimator IPD method combines information : Labeled data (true outcome, YY, model predictions, ff, available), Unlabeled data (model predictions, ff, available). Rather treating predicted outcomes importance true outcomes, method estimates data-driven weight, ω̂\hat{\omega}, applies predicted outcome contributions: β̂pspa=β̂classical−ω̂⋅(γ̂naivel−γ̂naiveu), \hat{\beta}_\text{pspa} = \hat{\beta}_\text{classical} - \hat{\omega}\cdot (\hat{\gamma}_\text{naive}^l - \hat{\gamma}_\text{naive}^u), $\hat{\beta}_{\rm classical}$ estimate classical regression, $\hat{\gamma}_{\rm naive}^l$ estimate naive regression labeled data, $\hat{\gamma}_{\rm naive}^u$ estimate naive regression unlabeled data, ω̂\hat{\omega} reflects amount additional information carried predictions. adaptively weighting unlabeled information, PSPA estimator achieves greater precision using labeled data alone, without sacrificing validity, even predictions imperfect. Let’s call method using ipd() function collect estimate slope X1 linear regression (model = "ols"): ipd_model S4 object slots things like coefficient, se, ci, coefTable, fit, formula, data_l, data_u, method, model, intercept. can extract coefficient table using ipd’s tidy helper compare naive classical methods:
code: set.seed(123) ipd_model <- ipd(   formula = Y - f ~ X1,   data    = dat_ipd,   label   = "set_label",   method  = "pspa",   model   = "ols" )  ipd_model #>  #> Call: #>  Y - f ~ X1  #>  #> Coefficients: #> (Intercept)          X1  #>   0.8801364   1.4324759 # Extract the coefficient estimates ipd_df <- tidy(ipd_model) |>   mutate(method = "IPD") |>   filter(term == "X1") |>   select(method, estimate, std.error)  # Combine with naive & classical: compare_tab <- bind_rows(naive_df, classical_df, ipd_df) compare_tab #> # A tibble: 3 × 3 #>   method    estimate std.error #> * <chr>        <dbl>     <dbl> #> 1 Naive        0.730    0.0145 #> 2 Classical    1.48     0.155  #> 3 IPD          1.43     0.146

title: Unit 03: BCR-ABL Fusion in B-Cell Leukemia
text: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia () common childhood cancer, exhibits marked genetic heterogeneity, distinct chromosomal translocations defining molecular subtypes divergent prognoses therapeutic responses. B-cell lineage , BCR-ABL1 fusion (“breakpoint cluster region”/“Abelson”, .e., “Philadelphia chromosome”) arises t(9;22) translocation encodes constitutively active tyrosine kinase. fusion historically associated poor outcomes, advent targeted therapies (e.g., imatinib) revolutionized treatment survival.   High-density microarray profiling measures expression 7,000 genes leukemic blast cells, enabling form “molecular diagnostics” supervised learning can: Classify fusion status genetic subtypes cytogenetic assays (PCR, FISH) unavailable. Discover novel marker genes pathways dysregulated specific fusions. Predict therapeutic response stratify risk using expression-derived scores. However, many retrospective multi-center cohorts, subset patients undergo gold-standard fusion testing (e.g., RT-PCR BCR-ABL1), leaving majority “unlabeled.” common workaround train gene expression classifier small labeled subset apply larger unlabeled cohort. Yet, naive downstream analyses, treating predicted labels ground truth, can yield biased effect estimates understate uncertainty. Inference Predicted Data (IPD) offers principled remedy: combines small labeled set predicted labels (e.g., true fusion status) larger unlabeled set, adjusting bias variance. module, : Describe Golub Bioconductor datasets. Subset data B-cell filter top 500 variable probes. Harmonize probes across platforms via gene symbols. Split data train three classifiers BCR-ABL1 fusion status. text: now use Inference Predicted Data (IPD) estimate log-odds effect sex (male vs female) true BCR-ABL1 status, combining holdout data true predict fusion status (.e., labeled data) Golub data predicted fusion status (.e., unlabeled data)  Insight: treating test set labeled Golub unlabeled, IPD combines information across cohorts correct bias improve precision estimating association BCR-ABL1 status patient sex. end module. hope informative! question/concerns/suggestions, please reach ssalerno@fredhutch.org
code: # Build labeled (ALL test) data frame df_test <- tibble(   sample = colnames(test_eset),   set    = "labeled",   true   = as.integer(test_eset$mol.biol == "BCR/ABL"),   pred   = as.integer(all_pred$testPredictions == "BCR/ABL"),   sex    = factor(pData(test_eset)$sex, levels = c("F","M")) )  # Build unlabeled (Golub) data frame df_golub <- tibble(   sample = colnames(golub_bALL),   set    = "unlabeled",   true   = NA_real_,   pred   = as.integer(golub_pred$testPredictions == "BCR/ABL"),   sex    = factor(pData(golub_bALL)$Gender, levels = c("F","M")) )  # Combine for IPD ipd_df <- bind_rows(df_test, df_golub) |> drop_na(sex) # Classical regression class_fit <- glm(true ~ sex, "binomial", df_test) class_df  <- broom::tidy(class_fit) |>   mutate(method = "Classical")  # Naive regression naive_fit <- glm(pred ~ sex, "binomial", df_golub) naive_df  <- broom::tidy(naive_fit) |>   mutate(method = "Naive")  # IPD logistic regression ipd_fit <- ipd(   formula   = true - pred ~ sex,   method    = "pspa",   model     = "logistic",   data      = ipd_df,   label     = "set", ) ipd_df  <- tidy(ipd_fit) |>   mutate(method = "IPD")  # Summarize coefficients combined <- bind_rows(class_df, naive_df, ipd_df) |>   mutate(term = recode(term, "sexM" = "Male (vs Female)"))  # Forest plot ggplot(combined, aes(x = estimate, y = term, color = method)) +   geom_point(position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +   geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = estimate - 1.96 * std.error,                      xmax = estimate + 1.96 * std.error),                  height = 0.2,                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.6)) +   geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +   scale_y_discrete(limits = rev) +   scale_fill_manual(values  = c("#1B365D", "#00C1D5", "#AA4AC4")) +   scale_color_manual(values = c("#1B365D", "#00C1D5", "#AA4AC4")) +   labs(     x = "Log-Odds Estimate (95% CI)",     y = "Covariate",     title = "Comparison of BCR-ABL1 Model Coefficients",     color = "Model Type"   ) +   theme_minimal()
